title: Cervical spine and muscle adaptation after spaceflight and relationship to herniation risk
summary: We would like to investigate what factors contribute to a higher risk of cervical disc herniation in astronauts as compared to normal population.

interventions.name: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the neck and upper spine, Cervical Spine 3d Kinematics, Maximal and submaximal voluntary contractions of the neck muscles, An endurance test of the neck muscles, Neck muscle fatigue test and questionnaires, Dual energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) examination of the
Control group will be investigated with the same protocol.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Any astronaut pre/post flight
Exclusion criteria:
Any non-MRI compatible metal implants or fragments
Any electronic implants (e.g. pacemaker)
Pregnant women
